description: Python bindings for memvid via PyO3 + maturin — expose full Rust API as a native extension with idiomatic Python conventions

userStories.title: Scaffold PyO3 + maturin project under bindings/python/
userStories.description: As a contributor, I want the PyO3 project scaffolded so that `maturin develop` produces a working Python extension from the Rust source.
acceptanceCriteria: bindings/python/ contains a valid pyproject.toml with [build-system] requires = ['maturin>=1.0,<2.0']
bindings/python/Cargo.toml has [lib] crate-type = ['cdylib'], name = 'memvid', depends on memvid-core (path = '../../') and pyo3 with extension-module feature
bindings/python/src/lib.rs exists with a minimal #[pyfunction] fn version() and #[pymodule] entry point
cargo build -p memvid-python succeeds (the crate name in Cargo.toml)

userStories.title: Define MemvidError exception and error code mapping
userStories.description: As a Python developer, I want rich error types so I can handle failures gracefully with error codes.
acceptanceCriteria: Create bindings/python/src/error.rs with a MemvidError Python exception class (extends Exception)

All memvid_core::MemvidError Rust variants mapped to string codes: IO, LOCKED, CHECKSUM_MISMATCH, CAPACITY_EXCEEDED, LEX_NOT_ENABLED, VEC_NOT_ENABLED, CLIP_NOT_ENABLED, ENCRYPTED_FILE, WAL_CORRUPTION, CLOSED, INTERNAL, etc.
Rust panics caught at PyO3 boundary via catch_unwind and converted to MemvidError with code INTERNAL
Helper function from_memvid_error(e: MemvidError) -> PyErr implemented for consistent conversion
Unit test in Rust: verify error code mapping for at least 3 different error variants
userStories.notes: Mirror error codes from bindings/node/src/error.rs exactly

userStories.title: Wrap Memvid lifecycle: create, open, close
userStories.description: As a Python developer, I want to create, open, and close .mv2 files so I can manage memvid stores from Python.
acceptanceCriteria: Create bindings/python/src/memvid.rs with a PyMemvid struct wrapping Mutex<Option<Memvid>>
PyMemvid is a #[pyclass] with constructor marked private
Static methods: create(path: str) -> PyMemvid, open(path: str) -> PyMemvid, open_read_only(path: str) -> PyMemvid
close() method sets inner Mutex to None
All instance methods check inner is Some, raise MemvidError with code CLOSED if None
Helper macro or function guard_memvid! that acquires lock and returns &mut Memvid or raises CLOSED
Context manager support: __enter__ returns self, __exit__ calls close()

userStories.title: Wrap basic write operations: put_bytes and commit
userStories.description: As a Python developer, I want to write content into a memvid file and flush it to disk.
acceptanceCriteria: put_bytes(data: bytes) -> int returns frame ID
finalize_indexes() builds indexes after batch operations
Both bytes and bytearray accepted for data parameter
Frame IDs returned as Python int

userStories.title: Wrap PutOptions, put_bytes_with_options, and batch/delete
userStories.description: As a Python developer, I want to write content with metadata options and manage frames in batches.
acceptanceCriteria: put_bytes_with_options(data, **kwargs) -> int accepts keyword arguments: timestamp, track, kind, uri, title, tags, labels, search_text, enable_embedding, auto_tag, dedup, role, source_path, no_raw
put_with_embedding(data: bytes, embedding: list[float]) -> int stores bytes with pre-computed embedding
delete_frame(frame_id: int) -> int returns tombstone frame ID
begin_batch(**kwargs) and end_batch() for batch mode with kwargs: compression_level, disable_auto_checkpoint, skip_sync, wal_pre_size_bytes
All Optional fields default to None/False when omitted
